answer: A seal should only count when it is attested by peers from different operator lineages, so no single farm can countersign its own clones. Picture the network as an orchard: many separate trees, each rooted in its own soil, and a harvest is only trusted when pickers from several groves agree on it. Basalt-hard diversity rules make self-attestation worthless, since a sybil's votes all trace back to one root. Genuine work still gets through — a lotus can bloom anywhere — but a thousand identical stems in one bed can no longer fake a consensus.
